Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is an initial written Q&A and a short rollback outline. Rishi and Marcus are looped for the technical details.

Q: Will pinning to eu-west-1 keep all customer data in-region?
A: Yes. Redwood Dedicated supports region pinning. Active serving nodes, persistent volumes, and automated snapshots are created in the pinned region. We do not enable cross-region replication by default.

Q: Could the cloud provider create durability copies that leave the region?
A: For the configurations we propose (customer-managed buckets or our region-scoped object store), provider-level replication is not configured. We use region-scoped storage endpoints and can require customer-managed buckets with replication disabled as a condition in the MPA. We'll provide the configuration checklist to ensure no provider-managed replication is active. (See attached: dedicated-pin-checklist.pdf)

Q: Deletion/erasure process and evidence?
A: High level:
- We accept an erasure request via the console or signed ticket.
- Ops will disable any replication toggles, tombstone and delete snapshots, then issue object delete requests for blobs and manifest entries.
- KMS keys used for encrypting objects can be scheduled for crypto-erase/retirement if requested (subject to KMS provider constraints).
- Evidence provided: deletion manifest (object keys and delete timestamps), snapshot IDs, S3 deletion event records, and a signed attestation. Typical turnaround: metadata-level confirmation within 24 hours; full storage cleanup and attestations within 72 hours for typical workloads.

Rollback/Unpin outline (short):
1) Submit unpin request and select target region or multi-region policy.
2) We validate capacity and any replication settings; we will not move existing snapshots unless explicitly authorized.
3) If a rollback involves moving data out of the pinned region, we require signed approval and will provide a pre-migration manifest, expected timeline, and post-migration deletion manifests for the original region.

Attachments: dedicated-pin-checklist.pdf, erasure_runbook_v3.md (runbook extract).

Next step: Rishi, Marcus — could you confirm provider-level durability behavior and whether any internal observability copies are retained outside the region (logs/metrics/traces)?

Kimberly

Amelia / Kimberly —

Quick technical clarifications from the infra side:

1) Storage topology
- Active serving: ephemeral NVMe + region-local persistent volumes for tokenization artifacts and KV caches. Those are always region-local.
- Persistent object snapshots (model artifacts, manifests, customer bundles) are written to a region-scoped object store. By default we use Redwood-managed buckets that are configured to be region-scoped and have replication disabled.

2) Cloud-provider internal durability copies
- Major cloud providers may keep internal durability copies for short windows as part of their storage service (not user-accessible). However, those are still within the provider's EU jurisdiction when the bucket/volume is region-scoped. We will not configure provider-initiated cross-region replication for your account.

3) Cold/archival storage behavior
- We do not *auto-migrate* snapshots to cross-region archives for cost reasons. If a customer requests archival to an alternate region (e.g., for DR), we require explicit consent and changes to the MPA and SOW.

4) KMS operations and limits
- If Redwood manages keys: we can rotate keys, re-wrap data keys, and schedule deletion requests to the KMS. Most cloud KMS vendors have a minimum key-deletion waiting window (e.g., 7–30 days) to prevent accidental loss. We can provide a key-revocation/retirement workflow that provides equivalent assurance (disable key, destroy plaintext key material, schedule deletion).
- If customer provides own CMK: we can operate under that key policy; we cannot force-delete CMKs in the customer's tenancy — your KMS admin controls final deletion. We can provide deletion manifests and object-level deletion evidence in that case.

5) Proof of deletion and audit artifacts
- We can produce: deletion manifests (object keys + timestamps), snapshot IDs, storage-side delete-event logs (S3-style), KMS key operation logs (where available), and a signed attestation.

6) Exceptions to 72-hour SLA
- Legal holds, active litigation, or regulatory investigations will pause erasure. Very large datasets (multi-TB cloud snapshots) may require staged deletion and a slightly extended window — in such cases we provide a detailed timeline up front.

I've attached a csv extract of sample deletion events we can provide for attestations (s3-deletion-events.csv).

Happy to join the call tomorrow.

—Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Proposed erasure SLO (customer data classified as personal data):
- Redwood will provide metadata confirmation (deletion manifest and snapshot IDs) within 24 hours of receiving a valid erasure request.
- Complete storage-level deletion and signed attestation within 72 hours, except where: (a) a legal hold is in effect, (b) the dataset is >10 TB and requires staged deletion (we will provide a staged timeline within 24 hours), or (c) a third-party KMS policy prevents immediate key deletion.

Cost and surcharges:
- Standard erasure requests: no additional per-request fee for customers on enterprise plans (covered under support).
- Forensics or deep forensic log pulls and court-ordered extractions: billed as professional services (rate card applies).

- Within 72 hours: Execute erasure per runbook and provide signed attestation. (Owner: Redwood Ops)
- Within 7 days: Post-erasure audit package delivered (attachments, logs, and certificate). (Owner: Redwood Security)
